findings: Date boundary hardcoding — Quarter and semester end dates use hardcoded day-of-month values. While correct for the specific months (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31), this is brittle if period definitions change. Use programmatic logic to derive the last day of each month instead.

TabRingkasan unaware of filter state — TabRingkasan receives no filter-related props and has no way to know which period is active, even though it displays filtered stats. If the component needs to display period metadata (e.g., 'Statistics for Q1 2026'), it cannot access dashboardPeriod. Pass dashboardPeriod as a prop for completeness.

Timezone mismatch in custom date filtering — HTML date inputs produce UTC-based Date objects, but response timestamps may be stored in local time (UTC+7). Boundary comparisons could produce off-by-one day errors, especially near midnight. Test custom range filtering with edge-case timestamps in the local timezone.

No filter persistence — Filter state resets to 'all' on every page reload. While consistent with the export filter, this may not match user expectations. Consider persisting to localStorage or URL params for a more persistent dashboard experience.
